DECISION HISTORY:

Creation of an outdoor exhibit for orangutans was an approved project for 2016-2018.
Design for this project was awarded to Balind Architect Inc. in 2016. Work on the
project stopped in the fall of 2017, and in spring of 2018, the Zoo learned that the
principle architect was no longer able to complete the project due to personal reasons.

position to award the detailed design and contract administration portion of this project
based on the results of RFP 58 (2018-10).

COMMENTS:

The Toronto Zoo issued RFP 58 (2018-10) Outdoor Orangutan Exhibit, inviting 15
experienced and qualified consultants to submit a written proposal to design an outdoor
orangutan exhibit. The Request for Proposals was posted on the Toronto Zoo internet
website.

SUMMARY:

This report recommends the award of a contract for consulting services for the Outdoor
Orangutan Exhibit, RFP 58 (2018-10).

RECOMMENDATIONS:

It is recommended that the contract for architectural, engineering and project
management services for RFP 58 (2018-10) Consulting Services – Outdoor
Orangutan Exhibit be awarded to Zeidler Partnership Architects in the amount of
$350,075.00, excluding HST.

FINANCIAL IMPACT:

This is an approved project under the Capital Works Program. Remaining funding
available for this project is $5,063,282 for the balance of design, construction and
commissioning.

DECISION HISTORY:

Creation of an outdoor exhibit for orangutans was an approved project for 2016-2018.
Design for this project was awarded to Balind Architect Inc. in 2016. Work on the
project stopped in the fall of 2017, and in spring of 2018, the Zoo learned that the
principle architect was no longer able to complete the project due to personal reasons.

The Zoo has terminated the agreement with Balind Architect Inc. and are now in a
position to award the detailed design and contract administration portion of this project
based on the results of RFP 58 (2018-10).

COMMENTS:

The Toronto Zoo issued RFP 58 (2018-10) Outdoor Orangutan Exhibit, inviting 15
experienced and qualified consultants to submit a written proposal to design an outdoor
orangutan exhibit. The Request for Proposals was posted on the Toronto Zoo internet
website.

Consulting Services – Outdoor Orangutan Exhibit                                  Page 1 of 2
Four interested vendors attended an on-site inspection or participated in a tele-
conference review of the project with the Zoo. Proposals were received from three
proponents (see Appendix I).

The proposals were reviewed and rated by an evaluation committee comprised of staff
members from Facilities & Services, Project Management and Purchasing & Supply.
Proposals were evaluated based on consulting experience on similar projects,
commitment to the schedule, understanding of the scope, proposed methodology and
cost.

At the conclusion of the evaluation process, the final results were tabulated and Zeidler
Partnership Architects scored the highest with a total of 78.9% out of a total 100.0
points available in the full evaluation process. No other proponents scored 70.0% or
higher in the process which is considered the minimum threshold for award.

Zeidler Partnership Architects’ proposal met all of the Zoo’s requirements and received
the highest scoring based on the pre-established evaluation criteria within the RFP.
Zeidler Partnership Architects and their assembled team for this project have related
experience designing and providing consulting services for orangutan and great ape
exhibits at other zoological facilities around the world, which will be most desirable for
the successful completion of this project. In addition, Zeidler stated that they can meet
the Zoo’s proposed schedule of design and construction for an orangutan exhibit
opening in 2020.

SUMMARY:

This report recommends the award of the request of proposal for a parking
management system replacement.

RECOMMENDATIONS:

It is recommended that the tender for the parking management system
replacement, RFP #21 (2018-04) – Parking Management System be awarded to
Precise ParkLink in the amount of $307,149, excluding Goods and Services Tax.

FINANCIAL IMPACT:

There is no financial impact to this report, as the funding is included in the approved
2018-2022 Capital Works Program (Information Systems Budget).

DECISION HISTORY:

The current Toronto Zoo parking management system was installed in 2007. It is
showing its age with continuing operational issues and requires an increasing amount of
service maintenance from year to year.

COMMENTS:

The Toronto Zoo issued Parking Management System - RFP #21 (2018-04), inviting
experienced and qualified service providers to submit a written proposal to replace the
existing parking operation equipment and software with a commercial off-the-shelf
parking system.

The RFP was posted on the Toronto Zoo website. Twenty-one interested vendors
attended the mandatory on-site inspection. Proposals were received from 7 proponents
(see Appendix I).

The proposals were reviewed and rated by an evaluation committee consisting of four
staff members from Member & Guest Services, Financial Services and Safety &
Security. Proposals were evaluated based on capability, technical merit, methodology,

and cost. This included a detailed review of 99–point general and functional
requirement criteria that proponents were asked to complete.

Following an initial evaluation of the seven proposals received, a short list of three
Proponents were invited to present and demonstrate their proposal to the evaluation
committee. Subsequent to the interview process, the final results were tabulated and
Precise ParkLink Inc. scored the highest with a total of 117.8 (78.5%) out of a total
150.0 points available in the full evaluation process. Only one other proponent scored
70.0% or higher in the process which is considered the minimum requirement for award.

Precise ParkLink Inc. has proposed a replacement parking management system that is
customer-centered and administratively and operationally effective. The system
recommended received the highest scoring based on the pre-established evaluation
criteria within the RFP submission and interview process, and met all of the
specifications. In addition, their proposal was the only solution that integrates
seamlessly with our existing ADMITS point of sale software.
